```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(geomtextpath)
```

An intro to geomtextpath

## Purposes {auto-animate=true}

::: incremental
- Extension of ggplot2
- Text can follow any path, and keep correct spacing!
  - Label lines
  - Label contours
  - Label roads and rivers on map plots
  - And much more!!!
:::

## To Use {auto-animate=true}


Simply download the package from CRAN and load it in along with ggplot2!


```{.r code-line-numbers="1-2"}
library(ggplot2)
library(geomtextpath)
```


## Core Functions {auto-animate=true}


::: incremental
- geom_textpath
- geom_labelpath

- *Works like any other geom in the ggplot2 package!*
:::

## Example {auto-animate=true}

```{.r code-line-numbers="12"}
t <- seq(5, -1, length.out = 1000) * pi

spiral <- data.frame(x    = sin(t) * 1:1000, 
                     y    = cos(t) * 1:1000,
                     text = paste("We,",
                                  "love,",
                                  "data,",
                                  "science!")
                     )

ggplot(spiral, aes(x, y, label = text)) +
  geom_textpath(size = 7, vjust = 2, text_only = TRUE) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-1500, 1500), ylim = c(-1500, 1500))
```

:::incremental
- *size: changes size of text*
- *vjust: changes how spaced out text is*
- *text_only: determines whether or not other elements are included, in this case, it is the defined "spiral"*
:::

## Example {auto-animate=true}

```{r}
t <- seq(5, -1, length.out = 1000) * pi

spiral <- data.frame(x    = sin(t) * 1:1000, 
                     y    = cos(t) * 1:1000,
                     text = paste("We",
                                  "love",
                                  "data",
                                  "science!")
                     )

ggplot(spiral, aes(x, y, label = text)) +
  geom_textpath(size = 9, vjust = .1, text_only = TRUE) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-1500, 1500), ylim = c(-1500, 1500))
```


## Example {auto-animate=true}

Use geom_labelpath instead to put text in a box!

```{.r code-line-numbers="12"}
t <- seq(5, -1, length.out = 1000) * pi

spiral <- data.frame(x    = sin(t) * 1:1000, 
                     y    = cos(t) * 1:1000,
                     text = paste("We,",
                                  "love,",
                                  "data,",
                                  "science!")
                     )

ggplot(spiral, aes(x, y, label = text)) +
  geom_labelpath(size = 7, fill = "#F6F6FF") +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-1500, 1500), ylim = c(-1500, 1500))
```

## Example {auto-animate=true}

```{r}
t <- seq(5, -1, length.out = 1000) * pi

spiral <- data.frame(x    = sin(t) * 1:1000, 
                     y    = cos(t) * 1:1000,
                     text = paste("We",
                                  "love",

                                  "science!")
                     )

ggplot(spiral, aes(x, y, label = text)) +
  geom_labelpath(size = 7, fill = "#F6F6FF", text_only = TRUE) +

```

## Data Example {auto-animate=true}

Every geom object has a geom_text and geom_label equivalent!

For this example, we will use geom_smooth. 

geom_smooth	= geom_textsmooth =	geom_labelsmooth

## Penguins {auto-animate=true}

```{r}
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) 
```

This is good... but what if we had the species name ON the lines?

## Penguins {auto-animate=true}

```{.r code-line-numbers="3-4"}
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_labelsmooth(aes(label = species), text_smoothing = 50, fill = "#F6F6FF",
                size = 5, linewidth = 1, boxlinewidth = 0.6) 
```

```{r}
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_labelsmooth(aes(label = species), text_smoothing = 50, fill = "#F6F6FF",
                size = 5, linewidth = 1, boxlinewidth = 0.6)+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

No legend necessary!!

## Penguins {auto-animate=true}

Can also be used with density plots. 

```{.r code-line-numbers="4"}
penguins |>
  filter(species != "Chinstrap")|>
ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g, color = species, label = species))+
  geom_textdensity(size = 4, fontface = 2, hjust = 0.2, vjust = 0.3)+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Notice that we JUST need the geom_textdensity layer to create the density plot!

## Penguins {auto-animate=true}

```{r}
penguins |>
  filter(species != "Chinstrap")|>
ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g, color = species, label = species))+
  geom_textdensity(size = 4, fontface = 2, hjust = 0.2, vjust = 0.3)+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Penguins {auto-animate=true}

Can also change *where* the text is on the line using hjust!

```{.r code-line-numbers="4"}
penguins |>
  filter(species != "Chinstrap")|>
ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g, color = species, label = species))+
  geom_textdensity(size = 4, fontface = 2, hjust = "ymax", vjust = 0.3)+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

What do you think "ymax" will do?

## Penguins {auto-animate=true}

```{r}
penguins |>
  filter(species != "Chinstrap")|>
ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g, color = species, label = species))+
  geom_textdensity(size = 4, fontface = 2, hjust = "ymax", vjust = 0.3)+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
